The evaluation answers the research questions of .

RQ1 (priors): the data-aware methods dominate generic geometry, and the measured accuracy frontier belongs to LAMM (ROI RMSE 0.9715); certified RB-SR at 1.0599 is descriptively 35--47\% below the geometric baselines and 20\% below direct CVAE generation under the shared protocol.
These are direct method-to-method gaps, not the Ridge-referenced Holm family.

Because the test identities are excluded from final retraining, these gaps show the learned sparse-to-dense map generalises the population-level control shape regularity rather than memorising training noses.

RQ2 (proposed method): the predeclared primary hypothesis passes---certified RB-SR beats its matched anchor on ROI RMSE (-1.30\%, d_z=-0.97) and target-relative new flips (-31.6\%, d_z=-2.51, 100\% win rate) with the certificate holding on every pair, while the edge-strain difference remains honestly unresolved (+0.00012).

This is a justified operating point, not universal dominance: ARAP keeps the fewest flips and LAMM the lowest error, and the post-hoc PCA-128 study indicates the certified architecture can trade toward LAMM's corner when capacity is unlocked.

RQ3 (mechanism): the residual proposal already contains useful corrective signal, spatial gating extracts additional accuracy beyond the fixed blend, and deterministic certification removes the gate-induced fold excess while retaining approximately 99.2\% of the residual correction.
The source-conditioning ablation confirms that the anchor uses the supplied identity.

RQ4 (deployment): the benchmark explains why Rhinoform ships the anchor synchronously and the certified refinement asynchronously, surfaces the applicability boundary, and locks browser behaviour to the released assets through 51 conformance checks.
Two points bound the interpretation.

First, RB-SR improves ROI RMSE only modestly over its own ridge anchor; its large advantage is over the geometric and CVAE baselines, and the deployed value of the residual is that it is certifiably admitted, not that it is large.

Second, the metric set is not tuned to flatter the proposed method: ARAP legitimately wins both regularity columns and LAMM wins accuracy, which is exactly why the contribution is framed as a justified operating point on a fair, field-standard accuracy--regularity benchmark rather than a universal winner.

The work is technically evaluated, not clinically validated: it visualises the desired change on the patient's own face and shows when a request leaves the credible geometric envelope, without claiming to predict surgery.

Rhinoform fills a concrete gap in current rhinoplasty-preview practice as a research prototype that enhances the established preview paradigm along five axes. (i) Functional: it replaces the static before/after image with interactive sparse-control editing. (ii) Performance: the protocol-controlled benchmark shows RB-SR lowers ROI RMSE below both geometric propagation and direct CVAE generation. (iii) Credibility: instead of a single ``after'' image, it surfaces live normal-flip, edge-strain and OOD instruments. (iv) Personalisation: source-PCA identity conditioning makes the same nasal edit produce a different dense response on different source faces. (v) Evaluation: it complements visual plausibility with a protocol-controlled deformation benchmark.

The contribution is thus a complex research prototype that enhances the existing preview paradigm with a transparent sparse-to-dense deformation engine, face-specific statistical conditioning, and live geometric credibility feedback.

design commits to an explicit accuracy-primary, regularity-constrained operating strategy: RB-SR admits the residual under a spatial risk budget rather than minimising flips, which is exactly why the regularity-oriented ARAP legitimately wins the regularity columns---a deliberate trade-off, not a defeat.
Several threats to validity are addressed directly.
The main anchor/residual ordering is not an artefact of clean controls: the anchored Ridge/RB-SR pair exhibits comparatively gradual degradation under the specified control perturbations ().
It is not an artefact of a metric set tuned to flatter the method: the same field-standard accuracy/regularity pair is applied identically to all methods, and ARAP wins regularity.
The Stage 1 and Stage 2 validation diagnostics show that the anchor is already a strong predictor and that the recoverable residual gain is small.

Finally, the claims are deliberately scoped---the work is technically evaluated, not clinically validated; all metrics are screening proxies in uncalibrated FaceScape units; and the normal-flip rate is a geometric-degeneracy credibility warning, not a human-perceptible threshold or a clinical safety guarantee.
Read this way, the transparent-anchor-plus-gated-residual pattern is a candidate approach for other sparse-control, safety-sensitive medical shape-editing tasks, not only rhinoplasty.
Rhinoform was developed to support morphology communication in rhinoplasty consultation.

The project combines a browser-based consultation prototype with a controlled sparse-to-dense nasal deformation benchmark, allowing interactive shape edits to be evaluated through the same accuracy and regularity metrics used offline.
The evaluation demonstrates four main findings.
First, data-aware conditioning is important for dense nasal reconstruction.

The learned methods recover the nasal ROI more accurately than generic geometric propagation, showing that the source identity and learned population structure carry useful information beyond the sparse handles alone.
Second, geometric priors remain valuable for surface regularity: ARAP provides the clearest low-risk endpoint, even though it gives up dense accuracy.

Third, the measured accuracy frontier belongs to a modern localized neural editor---LAMM, retrained under the identical protocol, is the most accurate evaluated method---but that accuracy arrives with markedly more fold-over and strain, degrades fastest under control noise, and comes without a fallback anchor, an applicability boundary or a fold certificate.
Fourth, accuracy and regularity behave as separable axes.

The best deployment choice is therefore a justified operating point on a measured frontier, rather than a single method that dominates every criterion; the post-hoc PCA-128 study further indicates that where the certified architecture sits on that frontier is a capacity choice, not an architectural ceiling.
This interpretation clarifies the role of the learned residual.

The hybrid and RB-SR results show that nonlinear residual structure exists, but the effect is small because the ridge anchor already captures much of the low-frequency response specified by the nine landmark controls.

The residual that remains is spatially uneven and can introduce geometric risk when admitted without constraint---and soft budgets alone did not bound that risk, which is what made the hard ridge-relative certificate a structural component rather than an accessory.

Certified RB-SR is therefore most useful as a controlled residual mechanism: it keeps the stability of the source-conditioned anchor while admitting residual corrections where the gate permits and the certificate holds.
These findings also explain the prototype design.

The default preview uses the ridge anchor because it is accurate, stable and exactly real-time, while the certified refinement is resolved asynchronously and replaces the anchor only when its certificate holds.
In consultation use, a small RMSE gain has to be balanced against the risk of rendering a geometrically unreliable preview with confidence.
The interface makes this trade-off visible through the risk read-outs and the applicability boundary, allowing edits to be accepted, scaled back or withheld according to the measured envelope.
The deployment contribution is therefore the translation from benchmark evidence into an auditable interaction design, checked by the released conformance battery.
This dissertation makes four contributions, mirroring .

First, it formulates nasal morphology editing as a registered sparse-control to dense-deformation task and evaluates eight methods---spanning classical geometric propagation, direct neural generation, and localized neural shape-space editing including a retrained LAMM---under one pre-specified protocol.
A fixed nine-landmark protocol expresses interpretable nasal edits, while the dense nasal ROI provides the evaluation target.
This gives the project a reproducible benchmark structure rather than treating the prototype as an isolated visual demo.

Second, it derives and defends certified RB-SR: a source-conditioned ridge anchor, a residual proposal, a learned spatial admission gate, and a hard ridge-relative fold certificate whose guarantee is structural.

The held-out test confirms the predeclared hypothesis---lower error and fewer new flips than the matched anchor, with the certificate holding on every pair---while honestly recording that LAMM leads raw accuracy and ARAP leads regularity.

Third, it builds a statistically disciplined evidence chain: identity-level paired inference with dual source/target clustering, Holm correction within the frozen primary and secondary families, an explicit four-tier evidence hierarchy separating primary, validation, post-hoc and supplementary claims, and a single unlocked test access.
Fourth, it implements a limitation-aware browser prototype whose behaviour is locked to the released assets through 51 conformance checks.
The interface presents semantic controls, full-head visualisation, risk read-outs and an exportable scenario record.

The system is positioned as a morphology-communication prototype: it gives patients and clinicians a shared 3D reference while exposing the boundary of the preview rather than hiding it behind a confident render.
Overall, the evidence supports Rhinoform as a controlled and auditable prototype for discussing nasal shape change.

The project does not establish clinical outcome prediction, but it does establish a measured path from sparse consultation controls to dense registered deformation, with explicit evidence for where the method is accurate, where it is regular, and where the preview should be limited.
The benchmark uses registered skin-surface meshes.
It contains no bone, cartilage, muscle, skin-thickness, scar-tissue or airway representation.
As a result, the system can model visible morphology change on the surface, but it cannot infer the anatomical mechanism that would produce a surgical result.
The evaluation is FaceScape-only, single-expression and based on uncalibrated units.
FaceScape is suitable for a registered-topology geometry benchmark, but it is not a clinical pre/post rhinoplasty dataset.
The results therefore do not make millimetre-level, cross-dataset or cross-expression claims.
The control protocol uses nine nasal landmarks, and the prototype exposes six semantic slider directions that map cleanly to those handles.
This keeps the interactive edits inside the benchmarked control space, but it leaves richer free-form editing, additional surgical manoeuvres and surgeon-specific plans outside the present study.
The residual gains are modest because the source-conditioned anchor is already a strong baseline and because residual admission is deliberately constrained.
The applicability statistic is a control-scale check against the evaluated range, not a calibrated density model or out-of-distribution detector.
Normal flips and edge strain are mesh regularity proxies, not clinical safety metrics.

The fold certificate is anchor-relative: it guarantees the learned pathway never folds more than the ridge anchor, but it neither guarantees absolute fold-freedom nor detects large reconstruction error, as the mandatory qualitative failure case shows.
The 100 test identities were excluded from final retraining but were not historically untouched during project development, and no independent external confirmation exists.
The reported result is therefore internal identity-disjoint confirmatory evidence, one tier below an external test, and the dissertation's claims are scoped accordingly.
No patient or surgeon user study is claimed.
The prototype has not been validated as a clinical planning tool, medical device or surgical-outcome predictor.
Its validated contribution is technical: a controlled morphology-editing benchmark and an interface that exposes the limits of the preview.
The main ethical risk is expectation inflation.
A visually convincing preview can shape patient expectations even when the underlying geometry is uncertain.
The prototype addresses this by using a conservative default, surfacing live risk read-outs and shrinking or rejecting edits that leave the benchmarked envelope.
A second risk concerns body image and vulnerable users.
A morphology previewer should support discussion rather than increase pressure toward aesthetic change.
Any real-user deployment would require careful study design, appropriate screening for vulnerability, institutional ethics approval and clear explanation of the system’s non-clinical scope.
A third risk concerns provenance and consent.
The current work uses a research face dataset under a single neutral expression and does not perform identity-transfer or photorealistic outcome prediction.
The evaluation is technical and does not include patient data or user-facing clinical claims.
Future work follows directly from the limitations identified above.
The current release does not include a committed end-to-end browser frame-time distribution.
The next step is to instrument the deployed interface and report end-to-end latency distributions across representative devices.
A formative consultation study should then evaluate whether the six semantic controls, risk language and export record improve shared understanding without inflating expectations.
The current gate uses global risk budgets.
A more refined version should measure where the admission boundary is most sensitive across the dorsum, tip, alae and radix.
This would allow the system to explain not only whether an edit is risky, but which nasal sub-unit causes the rejection or shrinkage.
The present benchmark is surface-only.
A stronger deformation model would incorporate bone and cartilage support, skin-envelope thickness and tissue stiffness.
Physics-informed or FEM-style constraints could then act as additional certificates on top of the current registered-surface metrics.
Such work would require paired data carrying sub-surface anatomical information.
The six sliders provide a deliberately restricted semantic interface.
Future versions could study additional nasal manoeuvres, asymmetric edits and surgeon-defined control handles while preserving the benchmark structure.
The key requirement is that any new control should remain measurable as a sparse-to-dense deformation task rather than becoming unconstrained sculpting.
With LAMM already retrained and evaluated inside the benchmark (), the next tier of external comparators follows the comparability protocol of .

ShapeFusion would extend the comparison to masked-diffusion inpainting with an explicit diversity-versus-fidelity axis, while NPHM and ImHead would probe whether implicit localized head spaces, bridged back to the registered topology, justify their registration overhead with better nasal response.

The LAMM result also sharpens a more interesting open question: since LAMM wins raw accuracy but loses regularity and robustness, and the admission layer of is mechanism-agnostic by construction, a certified LAMM---LAMM's prediction admitted through the spatial gate and projected under the ridge-relative fold certificate---is the natural hybrid to evaluate, asking whether the accuracy frontier can be imported into the certified envelope rather than traded against it.

Moving from morphology communication toward clinical planning would require paired pre/post clinical data, calibrated measurements, surgical-manoeuvre labels, prospective validation, ethics approval and regulatory review.
The present work provides the first technical layer for such a programme: a controlled benchmark and an auditable previewer that make the limits of the current evidence visible.

This appendix collects protocol material that supports the evaluation but is not required to follow the main evidence chain: the comparability protocol under which the localized neural 3DMM editors of could enter the benchmark as external baselines, and the reproducibility and code-availability contract behind the released assets.
The localized neural editors surveyed in are the nearest published neighbours of this task, so it must be stated exactly what would make them commensurable with this benchmark.

The common harness is fixed: a candidate must implement a map from a source ROI surface and the nine displaced protocol landmarks to a dense displacement field on the registered FaceScape ROI topology, be trained (or fitted) only on the training identities, have its nine landmarks hard-fixed before scoring, and be scored with the identical free-ROI RMSE, sub-unit, edge-strain and normal-flip metrics of .
Under that harness, the four editors enter at three distinct levels of adaptation cost.
Direct entry: LAMM (executed).
LAMM's native interface already is this task: displacements of a sparse set of control vertices steer a dense mesh output in one forward pass .

Retraining its autoencoder on the identity-disjoint FaceScape split with the nine protocol landmarks included in its control set makes it a drop-in row of the headline benchmark, with no protocol change.

This entry level was executed in the present benchmark round: the retrained LAMM appears in and is analysed in , where it sets the measured accuracy frontier while conceding the regularity and robustness axes to the certified pipeline.
Conditional entry: ShapeFusion.

A masked diffusion editor fits the harness by setting the manipulation mask to the free ROI vertices and the handle set to the nine displaced landmarks, so the model inpaints the masked nasal region conditioned on the controls .

Because sampling is stochastic and the model optimises plausibility and diversity rather than fidelity to one target, the protocol must additionally fix a sampling budget K and report both the mean-over-K and best-of-K error; the spread across samples then becomes an extra, well-defined axis---generative diversity versus target-conditioned accuracy---that the deterministic rows do not have.
Registration-bridged entry: NPHM and ImHead.

The implicit models require the longest bridge: fit the identity latent to the source scan, impose the nine displaced landmarks as a localized editing constraint (via latent or region-latent optimisation ), extract the edited surface by marching cubes, and non-rigidly register the result back to the FaceScape ROI topology before index-based scoring.

The registration residual must be measured and reported alongside, because it lower-bounds the apparent error of the mechanism; correspondence-free metrics (Chamfer distance, landmark error) should accompany the index-based ones so the bridge itself is auditable.

A further confound applies to all four editors: published checkpoints are trained on other corpora (NPHM's scan set of about 120 identities, ImHead's roughly 4K-identity corpus), so zero-shot use would conflate mechanism with training distribution; results should either come from retraining on the identity-disjoint split or be labelled explicitly as a transfer tier.
This section specifies the protocol under which each editor becomes commensurable.

Of the three entry levels, the direct level (LAMM) was executed in the present benchmark round; the conditional and registration-bridged levels (ShapeFusion, NPHM, ImHead) remain scoped as future work in .
The evaluation is built to be rebuilt, with a two-level access model that separates what any reader can verify from what requires licensed data.

At the public level, the released repository carries the committed pair-level metric records, the summary tables, and portable verification tooling: tools/reproduce.py verify checks source-snapshot and evidence manifests, while its replay mode delegates to tools/replay\_release.py.
That replay recomputes the frozen primary certified-RB-SR--versus--Ridge six-metric analysis and the supplementary PCA-128--versus--LAMM three-metric analysis directly from committed pair-level CSVs.
It does not claim to recompute every table, ablation, noise analysis or figure in the dissertation with one command; those remain traceable to their separate committed records.
These release-level headline numbers are therefore auditable without model inference.
The browser build is verified by demo/verify.mjs, whose 51 conformance checks are described in .
At the restricted level, full retraining requires the licensed FaceScape data, the upstream LAMM implementation and the restricted checkpoints; this boundary is documented rather than hidden.

Every artefact in the reported result tree carries a SHA-256 sidecar, the result-tree manifest pins the complete evidence chain, and the pre-specified protocol records a single test unlock (held-out access policy record, with fail-closed policy and access receipts for the classical, LAMM and RB-SR test reads).

Determinism is enforced through seeded Python/NumPy/PyTorch runs (training/global/bootstrap/noise seed 20260609; final split/pair seed 20260809), and the CVAE is evaluated at its deterministic prior mean rather than by stochastic sampling.
The project is available at https://github.com/Cecilialzq/Rhinoform.git.

The released repository contains results/ (the reported result tree with per-pair CSVs, summary JSON tables and SHA-256 sidecars), docs/final\_tables/ (the audited headline and supplementary tables), tools/ (public reproduce and replay scripts), demo/ (the static browser client, its released model bundle and the conformance verifier), and the release manifests that record source lineage and asset hashes and fail closed on evidence drift.
